Narcissus (plant) :: Description :: Phytochemistry :: Alkaloids :: chunk_0007
As with all Amaryllidaceae genera, *Narcissus* contains unique [isoquinoline](/wiki/Isoquinoline "Isoquinoline") [alkaloids](/wiki/Alkaloid "Alkaloid"). The first alkaloid to be identified was [lycorine](/wiki/Lycorine "Lycorine"), from *N. pseudonarcissus* in 1877. These are considered a protective adaptation and are utilised in the classification of species. Nearly 100 alkaloids have been identified in the genus, about a third of all known Amaryllidaceae alkaloids, although not all species have been tested. Of the nine alkaloid [ring](/wiki/Ring_(chemistry) "Ring (chemistry)") types identified in the family, *Narcissus* species most commonly demonstrate the presence of alkaloids from within the Lycorine (lycorine, galanthine, pluviine) and [Homolycorine](/wiki/Homolycorine "Homolycorine") (homolycorine, lycorenine) groups. Hemanthamine, tazettine, [narciclasine](/wiki/Narciclasine "Narciclasine"), montanine and [galantamine](/wiki/Galantamine "Galantamine") alkaloids are also represented. The alkaloid profile of any plant varies with time, location, and developmental stage.[[24]](#cite_note-Bastida-25) *Narcissus* also contain [fructans](/wiki/Fructans "Fructans") and low molecular weight [glucomannan](/wiki/Glucomannan "Glucomannan") in the leaves and plant stems.

Like the [classical planets](/wiki/Classical_planet "Classical planet"), Uranus is visible to the naked eye, but it was never recognised as a planet by ancient observers because of its dimness and slow orbit.[[28]](#cite_note-34) [William Herschel](/wiki/William_Herschel "William Herschel") first observed Uranus on 13 March 1781, leading to its discovery as a planet, expanding the known boundaries of the [Solar System](/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System") for the first time in history and making Uranus the first planet classified as such with the aid of a [telescope](/wiki/Telescope "Telescope"). The navy blue flag field with lettering and symbols in gold, represents the state colors of Oregon.[[4]](#cite_note-obb-4)[[5]](#cite_note-Shearer-5) The 33 stars surrounding the shield represents Oregon's admission to the Union as the 33rd state. Below the shield is written *1859*, the year in which Oregon became a state.[[4]](#cite_note-obb-4)

Oregon's flag is the last remaining state flag in the U.S. in which the obverse and reverse sides have different designs.[[6]](#cite_note-mw-6) [Paraguay](/wiki/Flag_of_Paraguay "Flag of Paraguay")[[7]](#cite_note-7) is the only country that still has a two-sided flag. Two-sided flags were previously more common, but have been reduced due to increased costs of manufacturing a flag with two different designs.[[6]](#cite_note-mw-6) On the reverse of the flag is a depiction, also in gold, of a [beaver](/wiki/North_American_beaver "North American beaver"), the [state animal](/wiki/List_of_U.S._state_mammals "List of U.S. state mammals") of Oregon.[[4]](#cite_note-obb-4)

For dress or parade use, the flag may feature a gold fringe. For standard use, no fringe is required.[[4]](#cite_note-obb-4) The ratio of the flag's width to its length is 3:5.[[8]](#cite_note-fotw2-8)

It is one of nine U.S. state flags to feature an eagle, alongside those of [Illinois](/wiki/Flag_of_Illinois "Flag of Illinois"), [Iowa](/wiki/Flag_of_Iowa "Flag of Iowa"), [Michigan](/wiki/Flag_of_Michigan "Flag of Michigan"), [Missouri](/wiki/Flag_of_Missouri "Flag of Missouri"), [New York](/wiki/Coat_of_arms_of_New_York "Coat of arms of New York"), [North Dakota](/wiki/Flag_of_North_Dakota "Flag of North Dakota"), [Pennsylvania](/wiki/Flag_of_Pennsylvania "Flag of Pennsylvania"), and [Wyoming](/wiki/Flag_of_Wyoming "Flag of Wyoming").

Hirono served in the [Hawaii House of Representatives](/wiki/Hawaii_House_of_Representatives "Hawaii House of Representatives") from 1981 to 1994, sponsoring many bills that became state law.

From 1987 to 1992, she was Chair of the Consumer Protection and Commerce Committee.[[15]](#cite_note-15)

The city is located on the [Huron River](/wiki/Huron_River "Huron River"). It was also the first Olympics for [Nepal](/wiki/Nepal "Nepal") as a republic, the [Marshall Islands](/wiki/Marshall_Islands "Marshall Islands") and [Tuvalu](/wiki/Tuvalu "Tuvalu"). [Mongolia](/wiki/Mongolia "Mongolia") and [Panama](/wiki/Panama "Panama") each won their first Olympic gold medal. [North Korea](/wiki/North_Korea "North Korea"), having symbolically marched with South Korea as one team at the opening ceremonies of the preceding three Games that it entered ([2000](/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") in [Sydney](/wiki/Sydney "Sydney"), [2004](/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics") in [Athens](/wiki/Athens "Athens"), and [2006](/wiki/2006_Winter_Olympics "2006 Winter Olympics") in [Turin](/wiki/Turin "Turin")), paraded separately this time.
